content:
maya: Heads up — getting reports that pages didn't fire for a customer-impacting deploy from earlier. I see alerts in Sentry but no pager dings. 

incident-bot: [automated] alert received: https://alerts.redwood.example/INC-20260318-314159 — severity: P1 — route: payment-ingress — attachments: 1 (filtered)

jordan: confirming — logs show incident-bot posted to #incidents but the message had attachments stripped. Pager gateway dropped it due to a new attachment filter rule pushed in the last deploy. :eyes:

chris: which deploy? I can roll back the filter change.

maya: deploy id: infra-deploy-20260318-22:07 (jackie rolled it), changed filtering logic in notify-proxy; PR #4821.

jordan: snippet from proxy log (truncated):
```
2026-03-18T22:08:12Z notify-proxy WARN attach-filter: payload_size=2048 attachments=1 rule_match=strip_all
2026-03-18T22:08:12Z notify-proxy INFO post-to-slack: channel=#incidents text="[REDUCTED]" attachments_count=0
2026-03-18T22:08:12Z pager-gateway ERROR deliver: missing_escalation_metadata
```
\noncall-ryan: I didn't receive a page. My phone shows a slack mention but not a pager. Our downstream pager adapter needs the attachment block to contain "escalation_id" — stripping removed that key.

chris: ack. looks like the filter is aggressive when payload_size > 1024. The intention was to strip large binary blobs, not structured metadata. PR changed the rule predicate.

maya: impact assessment: customers hitting payment gateway between 22:08-22:15 saw delayed manual triage. No transaction loss recorded, but on-call response latency increased ~9m. We need to restore reliable paging immediately.

jordan: mitigation plan: 1) revert filter predicate (hotfix) 2) re-send recent alerts with attachments preserved 3) add unit test for escalation_id propagation 4) patch pager-gateway to fallback to parsing body when attachments missing

chris: I'm pushing rollback now. Command: `kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/notify-proxy --to-revision=infra-deploy-20260318-21`

incident-bot: [automated] notify-proxy rollback started by chris — tracking id rb-1718923456-1

maya: while rollback runs, jordan please manually re-emit the active alerts so they produce pages. Use `alert-resend --inc INC-20260318-314159 --preserve-attachments` from the runbook.

jordan: on it. re-emitting and watching pager-gateway.

jordan: re-emit done. pager-gateway logs show delivery success for oncall-ryan and eng-infra-sig. :white_check_mark:

chris: rollback complete: notify-proxy at revision infra-deploy-20260318-21. Verified attachments now pass through. 

oncall-ryan: got the page. confirming escalation metadata present. Thanks.

maya: follow-ups: - add guardrail to reject PRs that change attachment predicates without unit tests - add an integration test simulating missing escalation_id - update runbook to include a detection query: `notify-proxy|filter:strip_all count_by(route) > 0 and missing(escalation_id)`

eng-infra-sig: +1 on guardrails. I'll open a ticket to track policy and test coverage.

chris: logging note: added temporary verbose logs for attach-filter to help troubleshoot any similar future regressions. We'll remove verbose flag after 24h.

maya: customer comms: support to notify affected customers that monitoring alerted and on-call engaged; no data loss; response latency was delayed — internal postmortem will follow.

jordan: quick PR diff that caused the regression (from memory):
```
- if payload_size > 1024: strip_attachments()
+ if payload_size >= 1024 AND contains_binary(attachments): strip_attachments()
```
The boolean `contains_binary` had a bug and returned true for nested json blobs.

oncall-ryan: recommended short-term: add a fallback in pager-gateway to look for escalation_id in message text if attachments absent. That buys time if future filters trip.

maya: agreed. Create that as a medium-priority ticket.

incident-bot: [automated] incident status changed to: mitigated — responders: maya, chris, jordan, ryan — duration: 7m24s

chris: thanks team. I'll follow up with the revert PR notes and link to the postmortem draft. :shipit:

maya: closing thread for now — reopening if we see recurrence.
